excerpt: White fleshed dragon fruit dragonfruit is a species type: pink skin dragon fruit variety, also sold or known as white dragon fruit or white pitaya. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from species type (no registered Philippine variety).

blocks.text: If you came here looking for white dragon fruit or white pitaya, this is the same dragon fruit. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [dragon fruit variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit dragon fruit fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Fusarium wilt](/diseases/fusarium-wilt), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Fruit ripens 4 to 8 weeks after flowering.
**Fruit:** Oval, 150 to 600 g, pink skin, white flesh with small black seeds.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the most commonly seen dragon fruit type worldwide. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant White fleshed dragon fruit dragonfruit

Pick a variety by the fruit your buyers pay for: its size, sweetness and flesh, and how regularly the tree bears. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is white dragon fruit the same as White fleshed dragon fruit?
items.a: Yes. white dragon fruit is another name for White fleshed dragon fruit. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of White fleshed dragon fruit?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
